transcript:
This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed
investing to full-service wealth management all in one place. No matter your investing
goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly. New York's governor says she's
appointing Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor to lead the investigation
into allegations of sexual assault at Cornell University. A woman who says she was assaulted
by seven students at a fraternity party in 2024 recently filed a civil lawsuit that prompted
the local district attorney to reopen his office's investigation. In a statement, Governor
Kathy Hochulp says newly released information raises serious questions about the previous
investigation done by university police and the local prosecutor. Felix Reichman-Kernow
is a freshman at Cornell. A lot of people are very angry at the administration, and
I think it's also brought a lot of people together in organizing and in solidarity.
I think more people are making sure they report things that they see. In her lawsuit, the
former student at Cornell says she was pressured into drinking alcohol, smoking marijuana,
and snorting ketamine before being assaulted. President Trump is campaigning for Republican
candidates in red states ahead of the November midterm elections. President is scheduled
to be in Alabama today, and PR's Daniel Kirchleben says Trump made an appearance yesterday in
Durant, Oklahoma. Trump's speech, which lasted nearly an hour and a half, covered familiar
ground like promoting Republican tax cuts and baselessly accusing Democrats of cheating
in elections. Friday, Trump will travel to deep red Alabama to speak, and Saturday he
is scheduled to speak in Ohio. That state, which has turned red or in recent years, has
tight Senate and governor's races this year. When asked by a reporter today why he's campaigning
in solidly Republican states like Oklahoma, he responded, "I won all of them by a lot.
I'm going there just to make sure." He added that he wanted to thank Oklahoma for voting
for him in three presidential elections. Danielle Kirchleben, NPR News.
Google says it has successfully deployed a research satellite into orbit, one it hopes
will pave the way for orbiting A.I. data centers. NPR's John Ruich reports.
The device is about the size of a refrigerator, and on board it has four microchips designed
by Google that are already in data centers on Earth. The satellite is part of a research
project at Google called Suncatcher because the big lure of putting data centers in space
is the nearly unlimited supply of free energy from the sun. Google plans to run A.I. workloads
through the chips, testing how they perform after the stresses of launch and while being
hit by space radiation, they'll also gauge how hot the chips get and how well they can
be cooled by radiator panels without wind or water to help. The eventual goal is to
launch constellations of similar satellites that will process A.I. workloads, communicate
by laser link, and function as flying data centers in space. And a note, Google is a
financial supporter of NPR. John Ruich, NPR News.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Long-term mortgage rates in the U.S. are at their highest level in nearly three years.
Freddie Mac says the average interest rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage has risen to almost
7.3 percent. It's nearly a full percentage point higher than the rate one year ago. Economists
point out higher mortgage rates can raise the monthly cost to borrowers by hundreds
of dollars. The National Association of Realtors says in August, the median sale price of an
existing single-family home in the U.S. was $429,000.
Twenty-one states are suing the Trump administration over its repeal of pollution rules involving
power plants across the U.S. NPR's Julia Simon says the Biden-era rules were meant
to reduce emissions from the burning of fossil fuels.
The 21 states in four cities argue their appeal, quote, "guts one of the country's most significant
climate protections," end quote, and will worsen the climate crisis. The Biden-era
rules would have required coal and new natural gas plants to install pollution control equipment
that would have significantly reduced carbon dioxide emissions. When the EPA announced
the rule change last month, they said in their announcement that greenhouse gas emissions
from power plants, quote, "have no material impact on climate change." That is false.
And pollution from power plants also impacts human health. The EPA says it doesn't comment
on ongoing litigation. Julia Simon, NPR News.
The commissioner of Major League Baseball says the league is not considering the idea
of playing a game in the Grand Teton National Park in western Wyoming. Commissioner Rob
Manfred dismisses the possibility in a letter. I'm Dave Mattingly in Washington.

topics.text: New York governor appoints Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor for Cornell sexual assault investigation
President Trump campaigns for Republican candidates in Oklahoma, Alabama, and Ohio ahead of midterm elections
Google successfully deploys research satellite into orbit to test artificial intelligence data center technology in space
Long-term mortgage rates in U.S. reach nearly 7.3 percent, highest level in almost three years
Twenty-one states sue Trump administration over repeal of Biden-era pollution rules for power plants
MLB commissioner says league is not considering playing game in Grand Teton National Park
